about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

events: Weekly US export sales were the best in seven weeks (all 2026/27), led by Vietnam; shipments slowed. Commitments run ahead of last year but behind the 5-year pace vs USDA (ADMIS).
A weaker dollar after the midterms and hopes of lower tariffs helped early in the week; equity weakness capped mill-demand optimism (ADMIS).

sugar.fundamental: India's crush started unusually fast in October (Maharashtra harvested early for the festival season), a bearish surprise after months of El Niño and weak-monsoon worries.
events: Early Indian production data triggered a sharp selloff in March raws early in the week; prices are holding near the low end of that move (ADMIS).

coffee.fundamental: Brazilian coffee is reaching the exchange: ICE certified arabica has risen for several sessions after a long decline, and the volume pending grading jumped to its highest since March, all from Brazil — the deliverability that has made Brazil the price setter now weighs on the nearby. Brazil's October exports were up about a fifth on the year while Colombia's output fell after heavy rain. Rains in Brazil's coffee areas help next year's crop.
events: Brazil's October green coffee exports up ~23% y/y; Colombia's October production down ~8% (ADMIS).
ICE arabica pending grading at its highest since March, all Brazilian — a lead on further certified-stock builds (ADMIS).
March arabica is pressing toward its September low; Vietnam's robusta harvest weighs on robusta (ADMIS).

cocoa.fundamental: Two forces pull against each other. ICE certified cocoa stocks keep building to their highest since May 2024, a sign supply is outrunning grindings. Ivory Coast port arrivals are well behind last year and the 5-year average, and West Africa is drying as the rainy season ends with El Niño in play, though a leading forecaster says the risk is smaller than the hype. Near term the stock build dominates.
events: March cocoa broke out of a four-month range to its lowest since June and is testing the 200-day average (ADMIS).
ICE cocoa stocks at their highest since May 2024 and still rising (ADMIS).
Ivory Coast cumulative arrivals far below last year and the 5-year average despite an earlier season start; weekly arrivals improving (ADMIS, Reuters).
